recipes.name: Spinach Quiche
ingredients_raw: 1 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and drained
1 (6 ounce) package herb and garlic feta, crumbled
1 (8 ounce) package shredded Cheddar cheese, divided

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Melt butter in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add onion and garlic and saute until lightly browned, about 7 minutes.
Stir in spinach, mushrooms, feta, and 1/2 cup Cheddar. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon mixture into prepared pie crust.
Whisk eggs and milk together in a medium bowl until combined. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour over the spinach mixture in pie crust, allowing egg mixture to thoroughly combine with spinach mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes.
Sprinkle the top with remaining Cheddar and bake until set in center, 35 to 40 minutes longer.
Allow to cool briefly before slicing and serving, about 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Spinach Quiche
raw_recipe.description: This spinach quiche packs lots of veggies, plus herbed feta and Cheddar in a deep-dish pie crust for cheesy deliciousness in every bite.

review.reviewBody:
As already mentioned before in the reviews, the measurements on this recipe are a little off. If baked as per recipe, the quiche will be too oily and will not fit into one deep pie dish. Instead, I suggest making 2 quiches! Keep the same amount of spinach/mushroom/cheese mixture and separate it into 2 portions. Use the 4 eggs and 1 cup of milk (can decrease to 3/4 if you like) and half of the spinach/mushroom/cheese mixture for one quiche, and the same for the other quiche. Only use 1 tbsp of butter instead of the 1/2 cup recommended as it is WAY too much butter if you stick to the recipe.
The quiches turned out delicious and had a beautiful colour to them! Since this was my first quiche, I was afraid it would be too watery, but it came out firm. Tastes great!
This was delicious. I used fresh mushrooms and skipped the crust. Divided batter into muffin tins, baked then froze them. They reheated great! My family loved them.

Why oh why can't there be a six star rating? Let me preface this by saying that I have never been a big fan of quiche. I told my husband I'd make one, so I found this recipe. This is not only the BEST quiche I have ever had; I'd venture to say it is one of the most delicious foods I've ever eaten. Next time, I will try to make it with less butter as others have suggested. I used plain feta and added a dash of oregano, basil, rosemary and seasoned pepper. I made the Pastry for a Single Crust Pie from this site, and it was great for this dish. (Probably not so great for a sweet pie). Anyway, thank you for the fantastic recipe Bailey, you are single-handedly responsible for finding a way to get my six year old to not only EAT spinach, but to eat it with gusto! I am in your debt. :)

Edited to add: If you ever plan on making this "healthier" by cutting back on the butter, I highly recommend you do it the FIRST time, so you won't be disappointed in the difference. It's still a good quiche with 1.5 Tbsp of butter, but it's a GREAT quiche with the whole stick. LOL

As so many others said, it's a very versatile recipe. I made 2 quiches and used 6 eggs, and 1.25 c milk. I kept the feta cheese at 6 oz but increased the cheddar cheese to 2 cups. I used the veggies I had one hand, which were a red and yellow pepper, 2 shallots, 6 cloves garlic, and an artichoke heart. I omitted the spinach and added 1 lb. of fresh bacon that I cooked and crushed. I pre-baked 2 frozen shells for 5 min at 375 then divided the veggie/bacon mixture in the 2 shells and then followed the cooking directions. Delicious!!

I craved quiche, and risked substituting many ingredients. I sautéed onions, garlic, green pepper, spinach, added deli mushrooms. Poured into crust, and placed sliced colby jack cheese on. gave a squeeze of dijon mustard, salt and pepper. Then used grated parmisan on top of egg mixture. THIS SHOWS THE GREAT DIVERSITY THAT THIS RECIPE OFFERS. Delish.

The best! I didn't have garlic or mushrooms so I omitted them. I used plain goat cheese and sharp cheddar ((about 1/2 C more than called for) I grated the onion, browned with a pinch of Italian seasoning, then baked in pre-baked homemade pie crust. DELICIOUS!
You only need 3 eggs and 1/2 cup of milk. 4 eggs and 1/2 cup will be too much for even a deep dish pie shell.

These are my modifications because of what I had on hand. I sautéed my sweet onions and butter.I used heavy whipping cream... 2/3 of a cup. I used a few more eggs because I like it thick .I added havarti cheese mixed with Munster cheese. I used chicken breast instead of the spinach because I didn't have any spinach on hand. I also threw in fresh, crushed bacon and a pinch of ginger paste. Sea salt and ground pepper. This is how my family likes it… You can use a crust, but I cover it with the pie cover or you can make it without the crust. I always make it with the crust, but I don't eat the crust. I don't like my quiche overcooked or burnt anywhere using the crustless version. Bon appétit!! Gina

I sauteed about 1 c. onions in 1/2 stick butter until almost done, added 8 oz. fresh mushrooms til juice is released, stirred in fresh spinach until wilted. Use home-made pie crust made with shortening (not oil!), put in 11-in. quiche pan. Used whole milk. Baked 35 min. for final step. Did not use feta cheese. Made 8 servings @ 8 oz.

I did cut the butter in half and I used fresh spinach. I also pre-baked the pie shell. Next time I make it, and there will definitely be a next time, I will also cut back on the cheese and mix the egg and spinach mixturess together before putting them in the crust. I will also add something to make it a little spicy. It may be helpful to note that a frozen, store-bought pie shell is significantly smaller than a standard pie pan that you make your own crust to fill. That may be one reason some people have too much filling and others have a perfect amount.

In all these years of cooking, I never made quiche despite often eating quiche elsewhere. So I took the plunge. First, I used all fresh ingredients. I followed the recipe with some tweaks. When I sautéed the chopped onions, I sprinkled them with Hot Hungarian paprika. I would have liked to add mushrooms but I had none. I used good quality cheddar and Jarlsberg cheese, chopping these to the same thickness as if they were shredded. The four eggs and milk were a little too much, but that might be because the pie crusts were not deep enough. The one mistake I made was I did not remove all the liquid from the feta. I will be more careful next time. So the quiche was just a little on the liquid side. However, the flavor was perfect with a bit of a bite from the Hot Hungarian paprika. Oh, I only use real HUNGARIAN paprika.

I have been using this reipe for several years and it is delicious. I prebake the pie shell. I use Mrs. Callenders deep dish pie shells and they are perfect for this recipe. I use 3 jumbo eggs. Milk mixture must be added slowly and allowed to filter down through the spnach mixture. Sometimes I have leftover milk/egg mixture. I save it to use making waffles. I make this recipe to serve at brunchs I catered.It is one of the most requested items.
I enjoyed this and w/o a crust! Less carbohydrates! It cooked up fine. Very good. I had some this morning for breakfast and last evening for dinner after tennis!

I liked this recipe very much. The only change I made was to use fresh mushrooms instead of canned. I added about 8 oz of small white mushroom slices to the onions and just let them cook down. It yielded more or less 4 oz. The results were delicious with a splash of hot sauce. I'll definitely be making this one again.

Always turns out delicious! A few things I have learned after making many times…. If I want this fresh for breakfast I start the day before. I sauté the onion and garlic in 2 tablespoons of butter (I don’t use the full amount noted in the recipe). Once the onions are garlic are soft I add the drained spinach and cook long enough to get rid of any moisture left in the spinach. I store the spinach mixture in the fridge overnight night. The next morning I crumble my feta in the bottom of my frozen pie shell. Next I add the spinach mixture and then top that with half of the shredded cheddar. Then I pour over the egg and milk mixture. My quiche typically overflows so you may only need 3/4 of a cup of milk with the eggs. If I can’t find the garlic and herb feta I just add Greek seasoning to my spinach mixture and eggs. Always a hit.
This was very good! I used 5 eggs instead of 4, and I used fresh spinach and mushrooms. I would like to try it with less butter, since half a cup seems like a lot of butter.

Wonderful. I added some chopped cooked bacon - 3 strips - and some marinated artichoke hearts (skipped mushrooms this time). Cut butter in half - also added one egg and 1/2 cup half & half for two quiche. The best ever.
My favorite!!!!! I add chopped water chestnuts for a little added crunch.
I love this recipe! I do cut the butter in half. By preference, I also add crumbled, cooked bacon. This is definitely my go-to quiche recipe!!
Easy to make. Really tasty
